title: The revision is ordered, starting with Bihar
what_changed: The Election Commission ordered a Special Intensive Revision "in the entire country", starting with Bihar, with the schedule for the rest of the country to follow. Only electors whose enumeration forms came back would be on the draft roll. The 2003 Bihar roll, from the state's last intensive revision, was treated as evidence of eligibility, including a presumption of citizenship. Anyone not on it had to give documents from an indicative list of 11, and the younger the elector, the more were needed. Those born before 1 July 1987 gave their own. Those born up to 2 December 2004 gave their own and one parent's, and those born later gave their own and both parents'. A new declaration had to go with every Form 6 for a new voter, and with Form 8 for anyone moving into Bihar. No name could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer, the Commission's officer in charge of the roll in each state.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala | CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

title: Bihar's schedule
what_changed: Enumeration, the round of forms, was set for 25 June to 26 July 2025. The draft roll was due on 1 August, claims and objections were open from 1 August to 1 September, and the final roll was due on 30 September 2025. Forms received before 25 July would go into the draft.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: The 2003 roll goes online
what_changed: The 2003 Bihar roll, with 4.96 crore electors, was put online. Anyone on it needed no documents. Anyone not on it could use a parent's entry in it in place of documents for that parent.
documents: CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

title: The Supreme Court hears the challenge
what_changed: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the 24 June order. It observed that the Commission should also consider Aadhaar, the voter identity card and the ration card, but gave no direction to accept them. This account of the hearing comes from the Court's judgment of 27 May 2026.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Bihar's draft roll
what_changed: The draft roll was published, and claims and objections were open until 1 September. No name was to be deleted from the draft without a hearing and a written order.
documents: ECI press release of 01.08.2025 (PIB)

title: The names left off must be published
what_changed: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish the roughly 65 lakh names left off the draft with the reason for each. The lists were to go up district by district, searchable by EPIC number (the number on the voter identity card), online and on panchayat and block notice boards. The public notice was to say that a claim could be made with a copy of Aadhaar.
documents: Supreme Court order of 14.08.2025

title: Political parties brought in
what_changed: Twelve political parties were made parties to the case. They were told to have their booth agents help voters file forms with any of the 11 documents or with Aadhaar. This account of the order comes from the 2026 judgment.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Claims after the deadline
what_changed: The Commission told the Court that claims, objections and corrections could still be made after 1 September and would be considered up to the last date of nominations. The Court directed the chairman of the Bihar State Legal Services Authority to have the district legal services authorities send para-legal volunteers to help voters and parties file them online. This account of the order also comes from the 2026 judgment.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Aadhaar becomes the 12th document
what_changed: The Court directed that Aadhaar be accepted as the 12th document, as proof of identity. The Court said it is no proof of citizenship, and the authorities remained free to verify each card.
documents: Supreme Court order of 08.09.2025

title: The Commission follows the order
what_changed: The Commission told the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar that Aadhaar is the 12th document, as proof of identity, and that it is no proof of citizenship.
documents: ECI letter of 09.09.2025 to CEO Bihar

title: Bihar's final roll
what_changed: The final roll was published with about 7.42 crore electors. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer.
documents: ECI press release of 30.09.2025 (PIB)

title: Twelve more states and union territories
what_changed: The revision was extended to Andaman and Nicobar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, on the June order with changes. No documents were to be collected while forms were filled in. The form asked instead for the elector's own entry, or a relative's, in the state's last intensive revision, and after the draft notices would go only to those who could not be linked to it. For every form not returned, the booth-level officer (BLO), the official who looks after the roll for one polling booth, was to record a probable reason (absent, shifted, dead or duplicate). The declaration with Form 6 was changed, and BLOs were to carry at least 30 blank copies of Form 6 with it.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Which old roll counts
what_changed: Each state's forms are linked to the roll of its last intensive revision, and the Commission fixed which year that was. Linking an elector to that old roll is called mapping. West Bengal, Kerala, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Goa go back to 2002. Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Bihar go back to 2003. Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh go back to 2005, and Arunachal Pradesh to 2006. Tamil Nadu has two, 2002 for 197 seats and 2005 for 37.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: The first Phase II schedule
what_changed: Enumeration was set for 4 November to 4 December 2025 and the draft for 9 December. Claims ran to 8 January 2026, notices to 31 January, and the final roll was due on 7 February 2026.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Assam gets a different revision
what_changed: Assam was given a "Special Revision" in place of an intensive one. Booth officers were to check house to house from 22 November to 20 December 2025, with a register already filled in for them. The draft was due on 27 December, claims ran to 22 January 2026, and the final roll was due on 10 February 2026. The pages read give no reason for the difference.
documents: ECI letter of 17.11.2025 to CEO Assam (instructions listing, eci.gov.in)

title: Anta gets its own dates
what_changed: Rajasthan's Anta seat could not follow the 27 October schedule because a bye-election was under way, so it was given its own. Enumeration started on 8 December 2025, the draft was due on 12 January 2026, claims ran to 11 February and the final roll was due on 12 March 2026.
documents: ECI letter of 27.11.2025 for 193-Anta, CEO Rajasthan

title: Every Phase II date moves a week
what_changed: All twelve states and union territories got one more week. Enumeration now ran to 11 December, the draft was due on 16 December, claims ran to 15 January 2026, notices to 7 February, and the final roll was due on 14 February 2026.
documents: ECI order of 30.11.2025, as published by CEO Goa

title: Lists before the draft
what_changed: Before the draft, Chief Electoral Officers were to give party booth agents the booth-wise lists of those absent, shifted, dead or duplicated. After it, they were to put the lists online, searchable by EPIC number.
documents: ECI press release of 10.12.2025 (PIB)

title: Seven move again
what_changed: At the request of their Chief Electoral Officers the dates moved again. Tamil Nadu and Gujarat got drafts on 19 December, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Andaman and Nicobar on 23 December, and Uttar Pradesh on 31 December. Kerala had already been moved to a draft on 23 December. The same release also lists Gujarat among the states keeping the 16 December draft, and does not name Puducherry.
documents: ECI press release of 11.12.2025 (PIB)

title: The "logical discrepancy" list
what_changed: The Court said names in the "logical discrepancy" category, flagged because something in their link to the old roll did not match, may be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices. Documents could be filed through an authorised representative such as a booth agent, the Commission was to allow ten more days from the display, and the Madhyamik admit card may be accepted.
documents: Supreme Court order of 19.01.2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025

title: More officers to help
what_changed: The Court had 8,505 state officers report to the district and registration officers to assist them, with the final decision left to the registration officers. Scrutiny was given at least a week beyond 14 February.
documents: Supreme Court order of 09.02.2026

title: Judges decide the claims
what_changed: Using its powers under Article 142, and with the parties' consent, the Court gave the deciding of claims and objections about inclusion to judicial officers of West Bengal, acting "for and on behalf of this Court". This account of the order comes from the Court's orders of 2 and 13 April 2026.
documents: Supreme Court order of 02.04.2026 | Supreme Court order of 13.04.2026

title: Judges from Jharkhand and Odisha, and no appeal to officials
what_changed: A further order set out the work given to the judicial officers and said their orders could not be appealed before any executive or administrative officer. Judicial officers from Odisha and Jharkhand joined those of West Bengal, and by 10 March there were 200 of them beside more than 500 from West Bengal. This account of the order comes from the Court's order of 10 March 2026.
documents: Supreme Court order of 10.03.2026

title: West Bengal's final roll, with 60 lakh held back
what_changed: The final roll was published with 60,06,675 names marked "under adjudication". They were to be added by a supplementary list if the judicial officers approved them.
documents: CEO West Bengal, press note CEO/PN-05/2026

title: Appeals go to tribunals
what_changed: No executive officer could hear an appeal against an order of the judicial officers. Appeals were to go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges, which the Commission would notify in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.
documents: Supreme Court order of 10.03.2026

title: Nineteen tribunals
what_changed: Nineteen appellate tribunals were at work. Appeals decided by 21 and 27 April were to take effect through a supplementary roll before polling, and a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
documents: Supreme Court order of 13.04.2026

title: The rest of the country
what_changed: The revision was ordered in 16 states and 3 union territories, covering the whole country except Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, whose dates would be announced later. Eight separate schedules were set. After the draft, notices would go to those who could not be linked to the last intensive revision (the no-mapping list) and to those whose link showed a discrepancy. Lists of those sent notices were to be published.
documents: ECI press note ECI/PN/086/2026 of 14.05.2026 (PIB) | Copy of the ECI order of 14.05.2026 (district site)

title: The Supreme Court upholds the revision
what_changed: The Court disposed of the petitions. It held that the revision has its legal basis in section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324, that it was proportionate, and that its document list, with Aadhaar added, was not arbitrary. The Commission may enquire into citizenship only for electoral purposes and must refer doubtful cases to the competent authority of the Central Government. People domiciled in Bihar whose names were wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may seek judicial review.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Mizoram avoids Sundays
what_changed: At its Chief Electoral Officer's request, Mizoram's draft moved from Sunday 5 July to 4 July 2026, and its final roll from Sunday 6 September to 7 September.
documents: CEO Mizoram press note of 04.07.2026 | CEO Mizoram press releases

title: Karnataka three weeks later
what_changed: Karnataka's draft came out on 24 August 2026 instead of 5 August. Enumeration ran to 17 August, claims to 23 September, and the final roll was set for 27 October instead of 7 October. It was published on 27 October.
documents: CEO Karnataka press note of 24.08.2026

title: Maharashtra four weeks later
what_changed: Maharashtra's draft came out on 31 August 2026 instead of 5 August. Claims were to run to 30 September, and the final roll was then due on 4 November instead of 7 October. On 26 September the Commission extended claims to 12 October and moved the final roll to 16 November.
documents: CEO Maharashtra press note of 31.08.2026 | PTI in ThePrint, 26 September 2026

title: Documents at the door, and a drive for those left off
what_changed: For people sent notices as unmapped or for logical discrepancies, BLOs would collect documents at home and upload them for the registration officer, so these people need not come to the office. A hearing would be held only in exceptional cases, as the registration officer decides, preferably online, and a family member authorised by the elector could attend. The Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the revision the forms in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply. Claims were extended in Delhi to 30 October and in Maharashtra to 12 October 2026. Where the revision was complete, in 20 states and union territories, anyone left out during it or after, and any young or first-time voter, could ask the registration officer to be added under continuous updation, and the Chief Electoral Officers, district officers and registration officers were to launch a special drive at once to enrol them.
documents: ECI press note ECI/PN/120/2026 of 26.09.2026 | ECI press release of 26.09.2026 (PIB)

title: Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya extended
what_changed: Andhra Pradesh's notices were to run to 10 October and its final roll was then due on 16 October 2026. On 14 October the Commission extended the notices to 22 October and moved the final roll to 30 October. Meghalaya's final roll moves to 26 October 2026, and it was published that day.
documents: ECI press release of 30.09.2026 (PIB) | Chief Electoral Officer, Andhra Pradesh, post of 14 October 2026 | Deccan Chronicle, 15 October 2026

title: The drive after the revision, in writing
what_changed: The Commission wrote to every Chief Electoral Officer setting out a special drive to enrol electors left off and young or first-time voters. Booth officers are to compare the current roll with the roll from before the revision, list everyone who was on the first and is missing from the second, visit them at home and help those found eligible fill in Form 6. The Commission asked them to cover at least 20 to 25 electors a week, so the work ends in about a month. The lists go to the booth agents of the recognised parties and then to the registration officer, who decides each case under the 1950 Act and the 1960 Rules. Booth camps are to be held, and special camps for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless. The letter says anyone not on the roll, or whose name was deleted, can apply to be enrolled at any time.
documents: ECI letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II) of 01.10.2026 to all Chief Electoral Officers

title: A drive to find the names left off
what_changed: When it published Uttarakhand's final roll, the state's Chief Electoral Officer set out the Commission's directions for what follows. Booth officers are to compare the roll from before the revision with the current one and list the electors who were on the first and are missing from the second. They are to visit them at home and help those still eligible fill in Form 6. The lists are to be shared with the booth agents of the recognised parties, and booth and special camps held, including for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless.
documents: CEO Uttarakhand, press note PN 63/2026 of 03.10.2026

title: A summary revision where the revision is over
what_changed: The Commission ordered a special summary revision of the roll, under section 21 of the 1950 Act, with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date, in 17 states and union territories. They are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. Polling stations are to be rearranged by 2 November, the draft rolls published on 12 November, claims and objections taken until 11 December and decided by 28 December, and the final rolls published on 4 January 2027. Claims for 1 April, 1 July and 1 October 2027 can be made in advance. No claim may be refused, and no name deleted, because a person cannot give an Aadhaar number. Recognised parties are to get each polling station's roll at the draft and at the final, on paper and as a readable PDF without photographs, with the lists of additions, deletions and changes, and a printed list of claims and objections every week. The registration officer must check deletions in person where they pass 2 per cent of a polling station's roll or one person has objected in more than five cases, and the limits on Form 7 set by the Commission's letter of 9 October 2026 apply. The letter says the dates for the states and union territories where the revision is going on or has just ended will be announced later. It names Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Sikkim, Telangana and Tripura. The dates for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, where the revision has not begun, are to follow with their weather in view.
documents: ECI letter No. 23/2026-ERS of 15.10.2026 to the Chief Electoral Officers of 17 States/UTs, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Final rolls moved in five states and Delhi
what_changed: The Commission revised the schedule in five states and Delhi on 29 October 2026, after requests from their Chief Electoral Officers. In Maharashtra, claims and objections run to 13 November and notices and claims are to be decided by 25 November. In Delhi, claims and objections run to 25 November, notices and claims are to be decided by 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December. Notices are to be decided by 20 November in Haryana and Andhra Pradesh, by 25 November in Nagaland and by 26 November in Telangana. The final roll in the five states is due on 30 November. The final rolls had been due on 30 October in Andhra Pradesh, 6 November in Haryana, 9 November in Telangana, 16 November in Maharashtra, 22 November in Nagaland and 4 December in Delhi. The revision came the day after the Supreme Court heard the petition on Delhi's revision on 28 October. At that hearing the Chief Justice told the Commission not to go by any cut-off date while no election was due in Delhi, and the press reported that the bench passed no order.
documents: The News Minute, 30.10.2026 | Business Today, 30.10.2026 | PTI in ThePrint, 29.10.2026 | ANI in the Free Press Journal, 30.10.2026 | Telangana Today, 30.10.2026 | Telangana Today (IANS), 30.10.2026 | Haryana Public Relations, release of 30.10.2026 from the Jhajjar District Election Officer | LiveLaw, 28.10.2026, on the Supreme Court hearing
